title: The Will of Greywater Bay
premise: Tamsin Kavanagh, a concierge at the Greywater Bay Grand who reads guests like tide charts, is hired by a grieving brother to find his sister, Elowen Marsh, missing for three weeks. The case turns strange when Tamsin discovers Elowen's diary contains entries written after her disappearance — in handwriting that matches her own. Following the diary's clues, he uncovers a thirty-year-old cover-up: four townspeople, now pillars of Greywater Bay, once let another girl drown to protect their futures, and Elowen had found proof. In the climax, the killer lures Tamsin onto the tidal flats at night; he survives by turning the town's loyalty against its liars, and the tide finally gives up both Elowen's body and the truth — though Tamsin must choose between exposing the last guilty party, an old friend of his own late mother, and letting the bay keep one secret.
about_author: Mara Oyelaran spent six years working front desks in coastal hotels before turning to fiction, a period she credits for teaching her that every guest carries an unwritten story. She lives near a tidal estuary, where she collects sea glass and writes mysteries about the things water refuses to forget.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Checked Out
chapters.summary: Tamsin Kavanagh's POV. At the Greywater Bay Grand's front desk, Tamsin notices everything — including that long-term guest Elowen Marsh hasn't touched her mail in weeks. When her brother Denny arrives asking Tamsin to find her, pride and curiosity make him accept. Beat: the hook of competence meeting its match.

chapters.title: Room 312
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Searching Elowen's abandoned room under a thin pretext, Tamsin finds a life meticulously ordered except for one drawer: newspaper clippings from 1994, a drowned girl's name, and a hotel keycard older than the current locks. Beat: unease beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: What the Tide Takes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The police call it a simple drowning or a walkaway; Tamsin walks the flats where Elowen was last seen and interviews locals who all repeat the same polished version of the town's history. Beat: the sense that Greywater Bay has rehearsed its innocence.

chapters.title: The Diary
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Denny produces Elowen's diary, recovered from her car. Its final entry describes a confrontation with someone powerful — then stops mid-sentence. Tamsin realizes the person she confronted is still alive, still local, and still watching. Beat: dread arrives.

chapters.title: Four Pillars
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The 1994 clippings point to four teenagers present the night Cressida Vale drowned: now the mayor, the harbormaster, the Grand's owner, and a retired teacher. Tamsin begins quietly probing each, cataloguing their alibis like reservations. Beat: the hunt becomes structural.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Thirty Years Ago
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: 1994, fifteen-year-old Cressida's friend Nell. A flashback chapter shows the night on the water — a dare, a storm, a boat that left without her — and the pact made on the dock afterward. Beat: sympathy for children who became liars.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. New diary pages appear in Tamsin's own mailbox, dated after Elowen vanished, in her handwriting. Either Elowen is alive and taunting him, or someone wants him to believe so. Beat: the ground shifts; the mystery turns personal.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin charms the harbormaster's estranged daughter into showing him old mooring logs: a boat went out the night Elowen disappeared, logged hours after it returned. Beat: first hard evidence, first real danger.

chapters.title: A Warning in the Lobby
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Someone ransacks Tamsin's staff locker and leaves a 1994 photograph with his mother's face circled among the onlookers. His employer, hotel owner Ada Voss — one of the four — offers him a promotion and a suggestion to drop the case. Beat: loyalty and threat entwine.

chapters.title: Nell
chapters.summary: Nell's POV, present day. Now the retired teacher, Nell watches Tamsin dig and wrestles with the pact she's kept since she was sixteen. She nearly tells him everything, then finds her own name added to a threatening note. Beat: guilt as a ticking clock.

chapters.title: The Mayor's Perfect Memory
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin traps Mayor Corliss in small contradictions about 1994 during a charity gala at the Grand. Corliss doesn't break — but afterward someone follows Tamsin home through the fog. Beat: the enemy shows its patience.

chapters.title: Denny's Version
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Digging into Denny, Tamsin finds gaps: Elowen's brother was in Greywater Bay the week she vanished and lied about it. Their sibling history holds an old wound over their mother's death. Beat: the client becomes a suspect.

chapters.title: Sea Glass
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell retrieves a hidden box from the dunes — Cressida's real diary, kept all these years — and reads what actually happened on the boat. She decides to give it to Tamsin, then hesitates when she learns who else knows it exists. Beat: courage gathering.

chapters.title: The Second Diary
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Nell leaves the box anonymously; Tamsin cross-references Cressida's diary with Elowen's clippings and sees it plainly: Elowen had reconstructed the drowning and blackmailed all four, gently, for money to leave town. Beat: motive crystallizes.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. An extreme low tide exposes the flats where Elowen disappeared; Tamsin finds her phone wedged in a channel marker, intact, which means it was placed there recently. Elowen may have been alive days ago. Beat: hope sharpens into urgency.

chapters.title: Ada Voss Explains Herself
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The hotel owner confronts Tamsin privately and confesses her part in 1994 — but swears she only paid Elowen to stay quiet, and that someone else among the four refused to stop at blackmail. Beat: confession without absolution.

chapters.title: The One Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Process of elimination narrows the killer to the one pillar whose alibi has never wavered because no one ever thought to check it. Tamsin sets a trap using a forged diary page hinting that Cressida's body was never where they think. Beat: hunter becomes bait.

chapters.title: Night Tide
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The trap works too well: Tamsin is ambushed on the tidal flats as the water rises, held by the killer — the harbormaster, who drowned Cressida deliberately in 1994 and silenced Elowen when she found out. Beat: terror, rising water, the price of noticing.

chapters.title: What the Bay Keeps
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, intercut with Nell's. Nell, following her conscience at last, arrives with Denny and the police just as the tide turns; the harbormaster is taken alive, screaming that the bay makes everyone complicit. Beat: climax and rescue.

chapters.title: Elowen's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The post-disappearance diary entries are explained: Elowen, hiding in the Grand's closed winter wing, wrote them herself to keep the pressure on — until the night she was caught. Her body surfaces with the spring tide, exactly where the diary predicted. Beat: grief arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: The Last Secret
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Among the evidence is proof that Tamsin's own mother helped cover up 1994 — the reason she left town and never explained why. Ada begs him to burn it. Beat: the theme made flesh; loyalty against truth.

chapters.title: Checking Out
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin gives the page about his mother to Nell instead of the police, choosing mercy without silence, and helps Denny bury his sister properly. He resigns from the Grand, keeping only the sea glass from Room 312's windowsill. Beat: resolution — truth served, family chosen.
